question: A 65-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 2-month history of intermittent bleeding from her vagina. She has no history of serious illness and takes no medications. Pelvic ultrasound shows a thickened endometrial stripe and a left adnexal mass. Endometrial biopsy shows a well-differentiated adenocarcinoma. Laboratory studies show increased levels of inhibin B. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Thickened endometrial stripe and left adnexal mass on pelvic ultrasound -> Endometrial biopsy shows well-differentiated adenocarcinoma -> Increased levels of inhibin B -> Granulosa cell tumor -> 95%

CHAIN: Intermittent vaginal bleeding -> Thickened endometrial stripe and left adnexal mass on pelvic ultrasound -> Endometrial biopsy shows well-differentiated adenocarcinoma -> Increased levels of inhibin B -> Granulosa cell tumor -> 90%
analysis: The most likely diagnosis in this case is a Granulosa cell tumor, which is a type of ovarian tumor that can produce inhibin B. The presentation of intermittent vaginal bleeding, thickened endometrial stripe, and an adnexal mass along with increased inhibin B levels point towards this diagnosis.
